name: dotnet-xunit

Author xUnit v3 tests for .NET 8.0+, covering `[Fact]`, `[Theory]`, data sources, `IClassFixture`, `ICollectionFixture`, `IAsyncLifetime`, parallelism, assertions, output, analyzers, and v2 migration.

Prerequisites: Test project already scaffolded via [skill:dotnet-add-testing] with xUnit packages referenced. Run [skill:dotnet-version-detection] to confirm .NET 8.0+ baseline for xUnit v3 support. See [skill:dotnet-testing-strategy], [skill:dotnet-integration-testing], [skill:dotnet-snapshot-testing].

| Feature | v2 | v3 |
|---|---|---|
| Package | `xunit` | `xunit.v3` |
| Runner | `xunit.runner.visualstudio` | `xunit.runner.visualstudio` (3.x) |
| Async lifecycle | `Task` | `ValueTask` |
| Assertions | Bundled | `xunit.v3.assert` or `xunit.v3.assert.source` |
| `[ClassData]` | `IEnumerable<object[]>` | `IEnumerable<TheoryDataRow<T>>` |
| `[MemberData]` | `IEnumerable<object[]>` | Supports `TheoryData<T>` and `TheoryDataRow<T>` |
| Assertion messages | Optional Assert parameter | Removed; use custom assertions or `Assert.Fail()` |

**v2 compatibility note:** If migrating from v2, replace `xunit` package with `xunit.v3`. Most `[Fact]` and `[Theory]` tests work without changes. The primary migration effort is in `IAsyncLifetime` (return type changes to `ValueTask`), `[ClassData]` (strongly typed row format), and removed assertion message parameters.

Use `[Fact]` for tests with no parameters. Use `[Theory]` for repeated logic with varying inputs: `[InlineData]` for simple values; `[MemberData]`/`[ClassData]` for complex or shared data. xUnit v3 uses strongly typed `TheoryDataRow<T>`; v2 uses `IEnumerable<object[]>`.

Fixtures provide shared expensive resources while preserving isolation. Use `IClassFixture` within one class and `ICollectionFixture` across classes. Implement `IAsyncLifetime` for async setup/teardown; v3 methods return `ValueTask` (v2 returns `Task`).

xUnit runs test classes within a collection sequentially and different collections in parallel. Each test class without `[Collection]` is its own implicit collection, so classes run in parallel by default. Place tests sharing mutable state in a named collection:
`[CollectionDefinition("Sequential", DisableParallelization = true)]`
**Do not disable parallelism globally.** Instead, group tests that share mutable state into named collections.

Create `xunit.runner.json` in the test project root:
`"$schema": "https://xunit.net/schema/current/xunit.runner.schema.json",`
Ensure it is copied to output:
`<Content Include="xunit.runner.json" CopyToOutputDirectory="PreserveNewest" />`

Use `ITestOutputHelper` for diagnostic output; it is per-test-instance. Bridge it to logging with an `ILoggerProvider` adapter when needed.

Create domain-specific assertions for cleaner tests. `Assert.Multiple` is available in v3; in v2, use separate assertions -- the test stops at the first failure.

Enable xUnit analyzers in all test projects. In `.editorconfig`:
`dotnet_diagnostic.xUnit1004.severity = suggestion`
Important rules include xUnit1004 (skipped tests), xUnit1012 (null value parameters), xUnit1025 (duplicate `InlineData`), xUnit2000 (expected argument ordering), xUnit2002 (value-type null checks), xUnit2007 (`typeof` checks), xUnit2013 (collection size equality), and xUnit2017 (`Contains()` on sets).

**One fact per `[Fact]`, one concept per `[Theory]`.** If a `[Theory]` tests fundamentally different scenarios, split into separate `[Fact]` methods.
**Use `IClassFixture` for expensive shared resources** within a single test class. Use `ICollectionFixture` when multiple classes share the same resource.
**Use `IAsyncLifetime` for async setup/teardown** instead of constructors and `IDisposable`. Constructors cannot be async, and `IDisposable.Dispose()` does not await.
**Keep test data close to the test.** Prefer `[InlineData]` for simple cases. Use `[MemberData]` or `[ClassData]` only when data is complex or shared.
**Enable xUnit analyzers** in all test projects. They catch common mistakes that lead to false-passing or flaky tests.

1. **Do not use constructor-injected `ITestOutputHelper` in static methods.** `ITestOutputHelper` is per-test-instance; store it in an instance field, not a static one.
2. **Do not forget to make fixture classes `public`.** xUnit requires fixture types to be public with a public parameterless constructor (or `IAsyncLifetime`). Non-public fixtures cause silent failures.
3. **Do not mix `[Fact]` and `[Theory]` on the same method.** A method is either a fact or a theory, not both.
4. **Do not return `void` from async test methods.** Return `Task` or `ValueTask`. `async void` tests report false success because xUnit cannot observe the async completion.
5. **Do not use `[Collection]` without a matching `[CollectionDefinition]`.** An unmatched collection name silently creates an implicit collection with default behavior, defeating the purpose.

References: https://xunit.net/; https://xunit.net/docs/getting-started/v3/migration; https://xunit.net/xunit.analyzers/rules/; https://xunit.net/docs/shared-context; https://xunit.net/docs/configuration-files
